name: deal_weave
prelude:
def weave : List α → List α → List α
  | [], ys => ys
  | x :: xs, ys => x :: weave ys xs
termination_by xs ys => xs.length + ys.length
def deal : List α → List α × List α
  | [] => ([], [])
  | x :: xs => let p := deal xs; (x :: p.2, p.1)
statement: theorem deal_weave (xs ys : List α) (h : xs.length = ys.length) : deal (weave xs ys) = (xs, ys)
proofs:
induction xs generalizing ys with
  | nil =>
    cases ys with
    | nil => simp [weave, deal]
    | cons y ys => simp at h
  | cons x xs ih =>
    cases ys with
    | nil => simp at h
    | cons y ys =>
      have e := ih ys (by simpa using h)
      simp [weave, deal, e]
  have balanced (as bs : List α) :
      (as.length = bs.length ∨ as.length = bs.length + 1) → deal (weave as bs) = (as, bs) := by
    induction as, bs using weave.induct with
    | case1 bs =>
      intro h
      have e : bs = [] := by cases bs <;> simp_all
      subst bs
      simp [weave, deal]
    | case2 a as bs ih =>
      intro h
      have hlen : bs.length = as.length ∨ bs.length = as.length + 1 := by
        simp only [List.length_cons] at h
        omega
      have e := ih hlen
      simp [weave, deal, e]
  exact balanced xs ys (Or.inl h)
strategies: Induct on xs, generalizing ys and consuming two heads per step.
Strengthen to balanced lengths and use the function induction principle for weave.
